import '@testing-library/jest-dom';
import { vi } from 'vitest';
import { act } from '@testing-library/react';

// Expose vi as jest so @testing-library/dom detects fake timers and advances them in waitFor/findBy
(globalThis as any).jest = vi;

// Polyfill File in jsdom environment if missing or unconstructible
if (
  typeof globalThis.File === 'undefined' ||
  !(function () {
    try {
      new (globalThis as any).File([], 't');
      return true;
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  })()
) {
  try {
    const { File } = require('node:buffer');
    globalThis.File = File;
    if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
      (window as any).File = File;
    }
  } catch {}
}

// Polyfill PointerEvent in jsdom environment
if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && typeof window.PointerEvent === 'undefined') {
  class PointerEvent extends (window.MouseEvent || Object) {
    pointerId: number;
    width: number;
    height: number;
    pressure: number;
    pointerType: string;
    isPrimary: boolean;

    constructor(type: string, params: any = {}) {
      super(type, params);
      this.pointerId = params.pointerId ?? 0;
      this.width = params.width ?? 1;
      this.height = params.height ?? 1;
      this.pressure = params.pressure ?? 0;
      this.pointerType = params.pointerType ?? 'mouse';
      this.isPrimary = params.isPrimary ?? true;
    }
  }
  (window as any).PointerEvent = PointerEvent;
  (globalThis as any).PointerEvent = PointerEvent;
}

// Polyfill scrollIntoView in jsdom environment
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
  if (typeof window.HTMLElement !== 'undefined' && typeof window.HTMLElement.prototype.scrollIntoView !== 'function') {
    window.HTMLElement.prototype.scrollIntoView = vi.fn();
  }
  if (typeof window.Element !== 'undefined' && typeof window.Element.prototype.scrollIntoView !== 'function') {
    window.Element.prototype.scrollIntoView = vi.fn();
  }
}

// Polyfill writable navigator.clipboard in jsdom environment
let _clipboard: any = {
  writeText: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined),
  readText: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(''),
};
function defineWritableClipboard(target: any) {
  if (!target) return;
  try {
    Object.defineProperty(target, 'clipboard', {
      get() {
        return _clipboard;
      },
      set(val) {
        _clipboard = val;
        if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.navigator) {
          try {
            Object.defineProperty(window.navigator, 'clipboard', {
              value: val,
              writable: true,
              configurable: true,
              enumerable: true,
            });
          } catch {}
        }
        if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined') {
          try {
            Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'clipboard', {
              value: val,
              writable: true,
              configurable: true,
              enumerable: true,
            });
          } catch {}
        }
      },
      configurable: true,
      enumerable: true,
    });
  } catch {}
}

if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.navigator) {
  defineWritableClipboard(window.navigator);
}
if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined') {
  defineWritableClipboard(navigator);
}

const origAdvance = vi.advanceTimersByTime.bind(vi);
vi.advanceTimersByTime = (ms: number) => {
  let result: any;
  act(() => {
    result = origAdvance(ms);
  });
  return result;
};

const origRunAll = vi.runAllTimers.bind(vi);
vi.runAllTimers = () => {
  let result: any;
  act(() => {
    result = origRunAll();
  });
  return result;
};

const origNextTimer = vi.advanceTimersToNextTimer.bind(vi);
vi.advanceTimersToNextTimer = (steps?: number) => {
  let result: any;
  act(() => {
    result = origNextTimer(steps);
  });
  return result;
};

```typescript
import React, { useState } from 'react';

interface CalculatorProps {
  initialValue?: string;
}

export function Calculator(props: CalculatorProps) {
  const [display, setDisplay] = useState(props.initialValue || '');
  const [history, setHistory] = useState<string[]>([]);

  const handleClick = (char: string) => {
    if (char === 'C') {
      setDisplay('');
      setHistory([]);
    } else if (char === '=') {
      try {
        // Safe evaluation of mathematical expression
        const sanitized = display
          .replace(/sin/g, 'Math.sin')
          .replace(/cos/g, 'Math.cos')
          .replace(/tan/g, 'Math.tan')
          .replace(/sqrt/g, 'Math.sqrt')
          .replace(/pi/g, 'Math.PI')
          .replace(/\^/g, '**');
        const result = Function(`"use strict"; return (${sanitized})`)();
        setDisplay(result.toString());
        setHistory(prev => [...prev, `${display} = ${result}`]);
      } catch {
        setDisplay('Error');
      }
    } else if (char === 'DEL') {
      setDisplay(prev => prev.slice(0, -1));
    } else {
      setDisplay(prev => prev + char);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div className="calculator" style={{ maxWidth: 340, padding: 20, background: '#13132a', color: '#fff', borderRadius: 14, boxShadow: '0 8px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.5)', border: '1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08)' }}>
      <div style={{ minHeight: 52, background: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.4)', padding: '12px 16px', borderRadius: 10, textAlign: 'right', fontSize: 24, fontFamily: 'monospace', marginBottom: 14, color: '#38d7f0' }}>
        {display || '0'}
      </div>
      <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(4, 1fr)', gap: 8 }}>
        {['C', 'DEL', '(', ')', 'sin', 'cos', 'tan', 'sqrt', '7', '8', '9', '/', '4', '5', '6', '*', '1', '2', '3', '-', '0', '.', '=', '+'].map(btn => (
          <button
            key={btn}
            onClick={() => handleClick(btn)}
            style={{
              padding: '12px 6px',
              borderRadius: 8,
              border: '1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06)',
              background: btn === '=' ? 'linear-gradient(135deg, #7c3aed, #06b6d4)' : 'rgba(255,255,255,0.05)',
              color: '#fff',
              cursor: 'pointer',
              fontWeight: 600,
              fontSize: 13,
            }}
          >
            {btn}
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      {history.length > 0 && (
        <div style={{ marginTop: 14, maxHeight: 90, overflowY: 'auto', fontSize: 11, color: '#64748b', padding: '8px 10px', background: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.2)', borderRadius: 8 }}>
          {history.map((item, idx) => <div key={idx}>{item}</div>)}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

export default Calculator;

```

#### `my-react-agent-lora/chat_template.jinja`

- **Path**: `file:///c:/Users/AYUSH/Documents/slm/my-react-agent-lora/chat_template.jinja`
- **Lines**: 54 | **Size**: 2,507 bytes
- **Description**: Jinja2 chat template for Qwen2.5-Coder formatting system instructions, user prompts, tool calls, and observations.

```jinja
{%- if tools %}
    {{- '<|im_start|>system\n' }}
    {%- if messages[0]['role'] == 'system' %}
        {{- messages[0]['content'] }}
    {%- else %}
        {{- 'You are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant.' }}
    {%- endif %}
    {{- "\n\n# Tools\n\nYou may call one or more functions to assist with the user query.\n\nYou are provided with function signatures within <tools></tools> XML tags:\n<tools>" }}
    {%- for tool in tools %}
        {{- "\n" }}
        {{- tool | tojson }}
    {%- endfor %}
    {{- "\n</tools>\n\nFor each function call, return a json object with function name and arguments within <tool_call></tool_call> XML tags:\n<tool_call>\n{\"name\": <function-name>, \"arguments\": <args-json-object>}\n</tool_call><|im_end|>\n" }}
{%- else %}
    {%- if messages[0]['role'] == 'system' %}
        {{- '<|im_start|>system\n' + messages[0]['content'] + '<|im_end|>\n' }}
    {%- else %}
        {{- '<|im_start|>system\nYou are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant.<|im_end|>\n' }}
    {%- endif %}
{%- endif %}
{%- for message in messages %}
    {%- if (message.role == "user") or (message.role == "system" and not loop.first) or (message.role == "assistant" and not message.tool_calls) %}
        {{- '<|im_start|>' + message.role + '\n' + message.content + '<|im_end|>' + '\n' }}
    {%- elif message.role == "assistant" %}
        {{- '<|im_start|>' + message.role }}
        {%- if message.content %}
            {{- '\n' + message.content }}
        {%- endif %}
        {%- for tool_call in message.tool_calls %}
            {%- if tool_call.function is defined %}
                {%- set tool_call = tool_call.function %}
            {%- endif %}
            {{- '\n<tool_call>\n{"name": "' }}
            {{- tool_call.name }}
            {{- '", "arguments": ' }}
            {{- tool_call.arguments | tojson }}
            {{- '}\n</tool_call>' }}
        {%- endfor %}
        {{- '<|im_end|>\n' }}
    {%- elif message.role == "tool" %}
        {%- if (loop.index0 == 0) or (messages[loop.index0 - 1].role != "tool") %}
            {{- '<|im_start|>user' }}
        {%- endif %}
        {{- '\n<tool_response>\n' }}
        {{- message.content }}
        {{- '\n</tool_response>' }}
        {%- if loop.last or (messages[loop.index0 + 1].role != "tool") %}
            {{- '<|im_end|>\n' }}
        {%- endif %}
    {%- endif %}
{%- endfor %}
{%- if add_generation_prompt %}
    {{- '<|im_start|>assistant\n' }}
{%- endif %}

```

# unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct

## Introduction

Qwen2.5-Coder is the latest series of Code-Specific Qwen large language models (formerly known as CodeQwen). As of now, Qwen2.5-Coder has covered six mainstream model sizes, 0.5, 1.5, 3, 7, 14, 32 billion parameters, to meet the needs of different developers. Qwen2.5-Coder brings the following improvements upon CodeQwen1.5:

- Significantly improvements in **code generation**, **code reasoning** and **code fixing**. Base on the strong Qwen2.5, we scale up the training tokens into 5.5 trillion including source code, text-code grounding, Synthetic data, etc. Qwen2.5-Coder-32B has become the current state-of-the-art open-source codeLLM, with its coding abilities matching those of GPT-4o.
- A more comprehensive foundation for real-world applications such as **Code Agents**. Not only enhancing coding capabilities but also maintaining its strengths in mathematics and general competencies.

**This repo contains the 0.5B Qwen2.5-Coder model**, which has the following features:
- Type: Causal Language Models
- Training Stage: Pretraining
- Architecture: transformers with RoPE, SwiGLU, RMSNorm, Attention QKV bias and tied word embeddings
- Number of Parameters: 0.49B
- Number of Paramaters (Non-Embedding): 0.36B
- Number of Layers: 24
- Number of Attention Heads (GQA): 14 for Q and 2 for KV
- Context Length: Full 32,768 tokens
  
**We do not recommend using base language models for conversations.** Instead, you can apply post-training, e.g., SFT, RLHF, continued pretraining, etc., or fill in the middle tasks on this model.

For more details, please refer to our [blog](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen2.5-coder-family/), [GitHub](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen2.5-Coder), [Documentation](https://qwen.readthedocs.io/en/latest/), [Arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12186).

## Requirements

The code of Qwen2.5-Coder has been in the latest Hugging face `transformers` and we advise you to use the latest version of `transformers`.

With `transformers<4.37.0`, you will encounter the following error:
```
KeyError: 'qwen2'
```


## Evaluation & Performance

Detailed evaluation results are reported in this [📑 blog](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen2.5-coder-family/).

For requirements on GPU memory and the respective throughput, see results [here](https://qwen.readthedocs.io/en/latest/benchmark/speed_benchmark.html).

````markdown
# Exact Steps: Fine-Tune a Code SLM for React + TypeScript + CSS

Tuned for your hardware: **RTX 4050 Laptop (6GB VRAM), 24GB DDR5 RAM**.
Base model: **Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct** (fits comfortably in 6GB with QLoRA; 7B is possible later via a rented cloud GPU using the exact same script).

Domain: React + TypeScript + CSS component/UI generation.

---

## Step 1 — Set up the environment

```bash
python3 -m venv slm-env
source slm-env/bin/activate

# PyTorch with CUDA (check pytorch.org/get-started if this doesn't match your driver)
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121

pip install unsloth
pip install datasets trl peft accelerate bitsandbytes
```

Verify GPU is visible:
```bash
python3 -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))"
```
Should print `True NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU`. Also check free VRAM before training:
```bash
nvidia-smi
```
Close browsers/other GPU apps before training — every MB counts on 6GB.

---

## Step 2 — Download the base model

```bash
pip install huggingface_hub
huggingface-cli login    # token from https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens

huggingface-cli download unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct --local-dir ./base-model
```

---

## Step 3 — Build your held-out evaluation set (BEFORE training)

Create `eval_set.jsonl` — 50–200 real examples of React/TS/CSS tasks you actually want the model to handle well. Each needs a way to check correctness (here: does the generated `.tsx` compile / pass a lint+type check).

Example lines:

```json
{"prompt": "Write a React functional component in TypeScript called `Badge` that takes a `label: string` and `variant: 'success' | 'warning' | 'error'` prop, and renders a styled span. Include a CSS module with class names for each variant.", "check": "tsc_and_render"}
{"prompt": "Write a React TypeScript component `Accordion` that takes an array of `{title: string, content: string}` items and toggles open/closed state per item on click. Style it with plain CSS (no libraries).", "check": "tsc_and_render"}
{"prompt": "Write a custom React hook `useDebouncedValue<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T` that returns a debounced version of the input value.", "check": "tsc_only"}
```

Base your real eval set on actual component requests you'd get in your own work — copy from real PRs/tickets if you have them. That's what makes the eval meaningful.

Save as `eval_set.jsonl`.

### Correctness checker for React/TS/CSS (Vitest + jsdom + Testing Library)
Unlike plain Python, "does it run" means "does it typecheck, render, and pass functional/a11y/interaction tests."

Install the testing harness dependencies:
```powershell
npm install -D vitest jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom @testing-library/user-event @vitejs/plugin-react react react-dom @types/react @types/react-dom typescript
```

`vitest.config.ts`:
```typescript
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
    setupFiles: ['./vitest.setup.ts'],
    css: true,   // handles CSS module imports without erroring
    globals: true,
  },
});
```

`vitest.setup.ts`:
```typescript
import '@testing-library/jest-dom';
```

---

## Step 4 — Build your training dataset

### 4a. Collect raw examples
Best source: your own repo's real components (strip out anything sensitive/proprietary before using). Pair a natural-language instruction with the actual component code:

```json
{"instruction": "Create a reusable Button component in React + TypeScript with primary/secondary/ghost variants, a loading state, and CSS module styling.", "output": "// Button.tsx\nimport styles from './Button.module.css';\n\ninterface ButtonProps {\n  variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost';\n  loading?: boolean;\n  children: React.ReactNode;\n  onClick?: () => void;\n}\n\nexport function Button({ variant = 'primary', loading = false, children, onClick }: ButtonProps) {\n  return (\n    <button\n      className={`${styles.button} ${styles[variant]}`}\n      onClick={onClick}\n      disabled={loading}\n    >\n      {loading ? 'Loading...' : children}\n    </button>\n  );\n}\n\n/* Button.module.css */\n.button { padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 6px; border: none; cursor: pointer; }\n.primary { background: #2563eb; color: white; }\n.secondary { background: #e5e7eb; color: #111827; }\n.ghost { background: transparent; color: #2563eb; }"}
```

If you don't have enough real components, generate candidates with a frontier LLM (Claude/GPT-5) via prompts like *"Write a React+TypeScript+CSS component for X, following common conventions"* — then validate every single one with the Step 3 checker before including it. Never include unvalidated generated code in training data; it teaches the model your generator's mistakes.

Other sources to mine (filter down to only React+TS+CSS, don't dump these in wholesale):
```bash
huggingface-cli download nickrosh/Evol-Instruct-Code-80k-v1 --repo-type dataset --local-dir ./raw-data
```

### 4b. Format into instruction pairs
One JSON object per line in `train_data_raw.jsonl`, same shape as above (`instruction` / `output`).

### 4c. Validate every example
```python
# validate_data.py
import json
from check_tsx import typechecks

kept = []
with open("train_data_raw.jsonl") as f:
    for line in f:
        ex = json.loads(line)
        # Extract just the .tsx portion if the output mixes .tsx + .css;
        # adjust this split to match how you format your examples.
        tsx_part = ex["output"].split("/* ")[0]
        if typechecks(tsx_part):
            kept.append(ex)

print(f"Kept {len(kept)} valid examples")
with open("train_data.jsonl", "w") as f:
    for ex in kept:
        f.write(json.dumps(ex) + "\n")
```
```bash
python3 validate_data.py
```

**Target: 300–800 validated examples** — for a narrow domain like this, quality matters far more than hitting a big number. A smaller, cleaner set will beat a larger noisy one.

### 4d. Cover the domain's real variety
Make sure your dataset spans:
- Functional components with props/state (`useState`, `useEffect`, custom hooks)
- Styling approaches you actually use (CSS Modules, plain CSS, styled-components — pick ONE and be consistent, since mixing styling paradigms in training data will confuse a small model)
- Common patterns: forms, lists, modals, conditional rendering, event handlers
- Accessibility basics if that matters to you (aria-labels, semantic HTML) — include it explicitly in examples if you want the model to default to it

---

## Step 5 — Fine-tune with QLoRA (Unsloth, tuned for 6GB VRAM)

Create `train.py`:

```python
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel
from datasets import load_dataset
from trl import SFTTrainer, SFTConfig
import torch

# 1. Load base model in 4-bit — 3B fits comfortably in 6GB VRAM
model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(
    model_name="unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct",
    max_seq_length=1024,       # shorter than default 2048 — saves VRAM
    load_in_4bit=True,
)

# 2. Attach LoRA adapters
model = FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model(
    model,
    r=16,
    target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj",
                     "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"],
    lora_alpha=16,
    lora_dropout=0.05,
    bias="none",
    use_gradient_checkpointing="unsloth",
    random_state=42,
)

# 3. Load and format your dataset
dataset = load_dataset("json", data_files="train_data.jsonl", split="train")

def format_example(example):
    text = f"### Instruction:\n{example['instruction']}\n\n### Response:\n{example['output']}{tokenizer.eos_token}"
    return {"text": text}

dataset = dataset.map(format_example)

# 4. Train — small batch size + more accumulation steps to fit 6GB VRAM
trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model=model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    train_dataset=dataset,
    dataset_text_field="text",
    max_seq_length=1024,
    args=SFTConfig(
        per_device_train_batch_size=1,     # small — fits 6GB
        gradient_accumulation_steps=16,    # keeps effective batch size reasonable
        num_train_epochs=3,
        learning_rate=2e-4,
        fp16=not torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),
        bf16=torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),
        logging_steps=10,
        output_dir="outputs",
        optim="adamw_8bit",
        lr_scheduler_type="cosine",
        seed=42,
    ),
)

trainer.train()

model.save_pretrained("my-react-slm-lora")
tokenizer.save_pretrained("my-react-slm-lora")
```

Run it:
```bash
python3 train.py
```

If you hit `CUDA out of memory`:
- Drop `max_seq_length` to 768 or 512
- Confirm nothing else is using the GPU (`nvidia-smi`)
- As a last resort, drop LoRA rank `r` to 8

Expect roughly 1–3 hours for 300–800 examples at 3B on this GPU.

---

## Step 6 — Merge the LoRA adapter

```python
# merge.py
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel

model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(
    model_name="my-react-slm-lora",
    max_seq_length=1024,
    load_in_4bit=False,
)
model.save_pretrained_merged("my-react-slm-merged", tokenizer, save_method="merged_16bit")
```
```bash
python3 merge.py
```

---

## Step 7 — Evaluate on your custom React/TS/CSS eval set

Use the Vitest + jsdom + RTL evaluation driver (`eval_custom.py`):

```bash
# Fast feedback iteration loop on a stratified 40-item subset (Batch mode, ~10s):
python eval_custom.py --model my-react-slm-merged --subset 40

# Full benchmark evaluation across all 153 examples:
python eval_custom.py --model my-react-slm-merged

# Sequential mode for live step-by-step debugging:
python eval_custom.py --model my-react-slm-merged --mode sequential

# Dry run / test harness pipeline without loading GPU weights:
python eval_custom.py --mock --subset 8
```

The driver automatically:
1. Enforces exact named exports in generation prompts (`Export the component as a named export called <Name>`).
2. Auto-binds named exports and provides fallback default export aliasing in test suites.
3. Splits TSX code and CSS modules into isolated test directories.
4. Validates TypeScript compilation (`tsc --noEmit`) and runs the full Vitest suite.
5. Reports breakdown pass rates across all 4 check categories:
   - `tsc_only`
   - `tsc_and_render`
   - `tsc_render_a11y`
   - `tsc_render_interact`
6. Exports full diagnostic error logs to `eval_results.json` for Step 9 retraining iteration.

Run this same eval set through three models to get your comparison:
1. **Base** `unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct` (un-fine-tuned) — baseline
2. **Your fine-tuned** `my-react-slm-merged` — did it improve?
3. **Claude/GPT-5** via API with a well-written prompt — the frontier comparison

For a more thorough check beyond "does it typecheck," manually review 15–20 outputs for whether they actually follow your intended conventions (styling approach, prop naming, component structure) — typechecking catches broken code, not bad style.

---

## Step 8 — Deploy

### Local (fits your laptop easily at 3B size)
```bash
python3 -c "
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel
model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained('my-react-slm-merged', max_seq_length=1024)
model.save_pretrained_gguf('my-react-slm-gguf', tokenizer, quantization_method='q4_k_m')
"

curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
```
```
# Modelfile
FROM ./my-react-slm-gguf/model.gguf
```
```bash
ollama create my-react-slm -f Modelfile
ollama run my-react-slm
```

### If you later scale to 7B on a rented cloud GPU
Same `train.py`, just change `model_name` to `unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct` and revert `max_seq_length` to 2048 and `per_device_train_batch_size` to 2 — the 24GB+ VRAM on a rented RTX 4090/A10 handles it without the tight tuning needed for 6GB.

---

## Step 9 — Iterate

1. Go through Step 7's failures — group them: type errors, wrong styling approach used, missed prop, ignored accessibility, wrong file structure (component vs. CSS split).
2. Write 20–40 new training examples specifically targeting your most common failure category.
3. Re-run Step 5 → Step 6 → Step 7.
4. Compare new pass rate + manual review quality against the previous run and against the frontier LLM baseline.
5. Repeat until you match/beat the frontier LLM on your eval set, or gains plateau.

---

```
Step 1 → environment set up, 6GB VRAM confirmed free
Step 2 → Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct downloaded
Step 3 → eval_set.jsonl written (real React/TS/CSS tasks, BEFORE training)
Step 4 → train_data.jsonl built from real components + validated with tsc
Step 5 → train.py run (3B, 6GB-tuned settings) → LoRA adapter saved
Step 6 → merge.py run → standalone merged model
Step 7 → eval_custom.py run → base vs fine-tuned vs frontier LLM
Step 8 → GGUF/Ollama local deployment (or move to cloud GPU for 7B)
Step 9 → analyze failures, add targeted data, repeat Steps 5-7
```

## 1. Project Overview & Architecture

Modern code generation benchmarks often focus on single-shot output: a model receives an instruction and outputs code. If the code has a missing import, a misnamed prop, or a failing edge case, it receives a score of 0.

Human engineers do not write code this way: they compile, read compiler errors and test assertions, diagnose the root cause, and iterate until all tests pass.

```
       ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
       │                       USER PROMPT                      │
       │    "Write a React TypeScript PinInputCode component"   │
       └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
                                   ▼
       ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
       │                   AGENT MODEL (3B)                     │
       │   1. <thought> (Plan & diagnose failure)               │
       │   2. <tool_call name="write_component">                │
       │        <tsx>...</tsx>                                  │
       │        <css>...</css>                                  │
       │      </tool_call>                                      │
       └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
                                   ▼
       ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
       │               AUTOMATED TEST HARNESS                   │
       │   1. TypeScript Compilation (tsc --noEmit)             │
       │   2. Live Vitest + Testing Library Test Runner         │
       └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
                    ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
                    │                             │
             [Tests Passed?]               [Tests Failed?]
                    │                             │
                   YES                            NO
                    │                             │
                    ▼                             ▼
       ┌─────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────┐
       │       <finish>          │   │      <observation>      │
       │  Verified completion!   │   │  Error trace & DOM dump │
       └─────────────────────────┘   └────────────┬────────────┘
                                                  │
                                                  └──► (Next Turn: Self-Correct)
```

---

## 2. Phase 1 — Foundations: Single-Shot vs. Agentic Loop

Initially, the project explored standard 1-shot Alpaca-style fine-tuning (`### Instruction: ... \n### Response: ...`).
- **Base Model**: `unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct`
- **Evaluation Benchmark**: 153 tasks (`react_ts_css_eval_set_combined.jsonl`) spanning forms, navigation, overlays, data tables, and custom hooks.

### The Problem with 1-Shot on 3B Models
A 3B model has high syntax capability but frequently trips on minor edge cases:
- Rendering `props.value` instead of `props.value || ""` (triggering uncontrolled input warnings).
- Forgetting an `aria-label="Digit 1"` attribute expected by `@testing-library/react`.
- Naming a prop `valueChange` when the test passes `onChange`.

In single-shot evaluation, these minor issues resulted in a **failed task**. Giving the model an interactive test loop with compiler feedback was necessary to unlock high pass rates.

---

## 3. Phase 2 — The Action Space Protocol: Why XML?

Standard function calling (JSON-based schemas like OpenAI Tools) failed consistently on 3B models:
- **JSON Escaping Hell**: Escaping double quotes, template literals (`` `${x}` ``), and multi-line strings inside JSON blocks caused frequent JSON parse crashes.
- **Context Waste**: JSON schema wrappers added 150+ tokens per turn of overhead.

### The XML Solution (`agent_protocol.py`)
We designed an XML tag-based action space:
```xml
<thought>
Explain reasoning, diagnose test failures, or formulate a plan.
</thought>
<tool_call name="write_component">
<tsx>
// Clean React + TypeScript code (no escaping needed)
</tsx>
<css>
/* Optional CSS / CSS module */
</css>
</tool_call>
```
When tests pass:
```xml
<finish>
Brief summary of the verified solution.
</finish>
```
The testing environment returns feedback via:
```xml
<observation status="failed">
[TSC]: Passed (0 errors)
[Vitest Test Failure]:
  × renders the correct number of digit inputs
    → Expected 4 inputs, found 0
</observation>
```

---

## 4. What Didn't Work: Failures, Bugs & Root Causes

During development, several critical failure modes were diagnosed and resolved:

### Bug 1: Unmasked Loss Dilution in SFT
- **Symptom**: The model was slow to learn self-correction logic and would often repeat test-runner phrases.
- **Root Cause**: `train_agent.py` was calling `SFTTrainer(dataset_text_field="text")` without token masking. Loss was computed across the entire conversation:
  - ~600 tokens of static `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`
  - User prompt
  - Large `<observation>` test output blocks (Vitest error stacks)
- **Impact**: On a 3B model with a small trajectory dataset, 70%+ of the gradient steps were wasted memorizing deterministic test-runner strings rather than learning code synthesis and error diagnosis.

---

### Bug 2: The "Hybrid" Non-Agent Dataset Contamination
- **Symptom**: When trained on `train_trajectories_hybrid.jsonl` (657 examples), the agent frequently output code directly inside `<finish>` without ever calling `write_component`.
- **Root Cause**: Upon inspection, 350 out of 657 examples (53.3%) in `train_trajectories_hybrid.jsonl` were legacy 3-message examples (`hybrid_ts_*`):
  ```xml
  <thought>
  I will write the TypeScript solution.
  </thought>
  <finish>
  ```typescript
  import path from "path";
  export default ...
  ```
  </finish>
  ```
- **Impact**: The model was rewarded for bypassing the test harness entirely. It treated `<finish>` as a markdown code block, directly violating the agentic tool-use protocol.

---

### Bug 3: Benchmark Eval Set Data Leakage
- **Symptom**: Suspiciously high 1-shot pass rates during initial evaluation.
- **Root Cause**: 164 of the 307 valid agent trajectories in `train_trajectories_hybrid.jsonl` had prompts identical to the 153 benchmark tasks in `react_ts_css_eval_set_combined.jsonl`.
- **Impact**: The evaluation was measuring memorization rather than true out-of-distribution reasoning and self-correction.

---

### Bug 4: TypeScript Duplicate Declaration Crash (`TS2440`)
- **Symptom**: During early STaR generation runs on `star_task_bank.jsonl`, **100% of tasks failed on Turn 1** with compiler errors like:
  ```
  TS2440: Import declaration conflicts with local declaration of 'PinInputCode'.
  Cannot redeclare block-scoped variable 'PinInputCode'.
  ```
- **Root Cause**:
  - `eval_custom.py` automatically generated component bindings:
    ```typescript
    import * as __Mod from './Component';
    const PinInputCode = (__Mod as any).PinInputCode ?? (__Mod as any).default;
    ```
  - Meanwhile, the test code written in `star_task_bank.jsonl` had top-level imports:
    ```typescript
    import { PinInputCode } from './Component';
    ```
  - When concatenated into `Component.test.tsx`, TypeScript crashed before running Vitest.
  - Because the model can only write `Component.tsx` and cannot edit `Component.test.tsx`, it became stuck in an unresolvable loop.

---

### Bug 5: Placeholder / Dummy Trajectory Harvesting
- **Symptom**: Harvested STaR files had tiny file sizes and missing code.
- **Root Cause**: `generate_star_trajectories.py` had placeholder rollout logic:
  ```python
  # Old code:
  history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": "// Verified implementation"})
  ```
  It was discarding the agent's actual generated TSX, CSS, and intermediate repair turns.

---

### Bug 6: `UnboundLocalError` Crash on Clean Passes
- **Symptom**: In the middle of an overnight 150-task STaR run, the pipeline crashed at Task #12 (`ProgressStepBar`) with:
  ```
  UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'regress_warn' where it is not associated with a value
  ```
- **Root Cause**: In `agent_loop.py`, `regress_warn` was defined only inside the test-failure `else:` block:
  ```python
  if passed:
      final_passed = True
  else:
      regress_warn = "..."
  # Later:
  if regress_warn and "</observation>" in obs: # <-- Crashed when passed=True!
  ```

---

## 5. What Worked: Systematic Fixes & Engineering Solutions

### Fix 1: Response-Only Loss Masking
In `train_agent.py`, we integrated Unsloth's response-only loss masking:
```python
from unsloth.chat_templates import train_on_responses_only

trainer = train_on_responses_only(
    trainer,
    instruction_part="<|im_start|>user\n",
    response_part="<|im_start|>assistant\n",
)
```
- **Result**: Tokens in the system prompt, user prompt, and `<observation>` blocks are assigned a label of `-100` (ignored by cross-entropy loss).
- **Benefit**: 100% of the model's limited 3B capacity is dedicated to generating high-quality `<thought>`, `<tool_call>`, and `<finish>` tokens.

---

### Fix 2: Universal Test Import Sanitization
In `eval_custom.py`, we introduced `strip_test_imports()`:
```python
def strip_test_imports(code: str) -> str:
    # 1. Strip import ... from './Component', 'vitest', '@testing-library/*', 'react'
    import_from_pattern = r'import\s+[\s\S]*?from\s*[\'"][^\'"]+[\'"];?'
    cleaned = re.sub(import_from_pattern, repl_from, code)
    # 2. Strip side-effect imports like import '@testing-library/jest-dom';
    side_pattern = r'import\s+[\'"][^\'"]+[\'"];?'
    return re.sub(side_pattern, repl_side, cleaned).strip()
```
And updated the test harness template to auto-inject standard bindings and React hooks:
```typescript
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef, useMemo, useCallback } from 'react';
import { render, screen, fireEvent, act, renderHook, waitFor, within } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { vi, describe, it, test, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import '@testing-library/jest-dom';

import * as __Mod from './Component';

// Injected component bindings
const PinInputCode = (__Mod as any).PinInputCode ?? (__Mod as any).default;

// Sanitized test cases start here cleanly
describe('PinInputCode Component', () => { ... });
```
- **Result**: Eliminated `TS2440` duplicate declaration crashes across all test suites.

---

### Fix 3: Anti-Stuck Escalation & Regression Guarding
In `agent_loop.py`, we implemented dynamic sampling intervention:
- If the model generates identical TSX or repeats the exact same test failure:
  1. `stuck_turns` increments.
  2. Temperature escalates (`0.20` → `0.55` → `0.90`).
  3. Repetition penalty escalates (`1.05` → `1.15` → `1.30`).
  4. An explicit intervention note is injected into the next observation:
     `"[ANTI-STUCK INTERVENTION]: Your previous attempt repeated the same failure. Alter your implementation logic."`
- When code or error state changes, sampling immediately resets to base values.

---

### Fix 4: Protocol Guidelines Injection
In both `agent_protocol.py` and `agent_loop.py`, we codified three recurring UI component patterns:
1. **Prop Fallback Aliasing**:
   `const trendVal = props.trend ?? props.valueChange ?? props.change;`
   `const initial = props.initialValues ?? props.initialState ?? props.defaultValues ?? {};`
2. **Minimal Clean Logging Rule**:
   When asked to log an action (e.g. `dispatchLogged`), output `console.log(action)` with no prepended label strings.
3. **Imperative DOM Dynamic Container Pattern**:
   Imperative hooks (`useConfirm`, `useToast`) must dynamically create and mount a container `<div>` to `document.body` if no portal root is provided in JSX.

---

### Fix 5: Incremental Flushing & Pipeline Resumption
In `generate_star_trajectories.py`:
- **Immediate Disk Flush**: Every passing rollout is appended and flushed to `star_trajectories.jsonl` immediately. If a run is interrupted, no passing rollouts are lost.
- **Resume Flag (`--resume`)**: The script reads existing task IDs from `star_trajectories.jsonl` and automatically skips completed tasks.
- **Fixed `regress_warn`**: Initialized `regress_warn = ""` alongside `anti_stuck_note = ""` to prevent runtime variable errors.

---

## 8. Phase 5 — Clean Training Corpus & SFT Training

### Dataset Assembly via `build_clean_dataset()`
To prevent the model from unlearning earlier capabilities while eliminating leaked and corrupted examples, we ran `build_clean_dataset()` across both sources:

```
[Legacy train_trajectories_hybrid.jsonl (657)]  +  [Fresh star_trajectories.jsonl (102)]
                                     │
                                     ▼
                       build_clean_dataset() Filter
         ├── Rejects 350 non-agent examples (code in <finish>)
         ├── Rejects 164 eval-set duplicates (prevents benchmark leakage)
         └── Deduplicates 99 identical prompts
                                     │
                                     ▼
             train_trajectories_agentic.jsonl (146 Clean Trajectories)
```

### Final Dataset Verification
- **Total Trajectories**: **146**
- **Protocol Compliance**: **100%** (all have `<thought>`, `<tool_call name="write_component">`, live test observations, and end with `<finish>`).
- **Eval Set Leakage**: **0 examples** (100% held-out).

### Completed SFT Training Run (Epochs: 3, LR: 1e-4)
With `train_trajectories_agentic.jsonl` assembled (146 trajectories), training was executed on the RTX 4050 GPU using response-only loss masking:
```powershell
python train_agent.py --epochs 3 --learning-rate 1e-4
```
- **Base Model**: `./base-model` (`unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct` 4-bit)
- **LoRA Targets**: `q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj` (rank=16, alpha=16, dropout=0.05)
- **Total Steps**: 96 steps across 3 epochs (batch size=1, gradient accumulation=4)
- **Loss Masking**: `train_on_responses_only` active (loss computed solely on assistant turns)
- **Convergence Metrics**:
  - Training loss dropped from **`0.9757`** (Step 5) → **`0.2930`** (Step 96).
  - Validation loss dropped steadily: **`0.5053`** (Step 25) → **`0.3848`** (Step 50) → **`0.3538`** (Step 75) → **`0.3503`** (Step 96, Best Metric).
- **Saved Model**: The best checkpoint (`checkpoint-96`, eval loss = 0.3503) was automatically saved to [`my-react-agent-lora`](file:///c:/Users/AYUSH/Documents/slm/my-react-agent-lora).
- **Output Artifact**: Ready for full evaluation on the held-out 153 benchmark tasks via `agent_loop.py`.

## 9. Phase 6 — Final Benchmark Evaluation & Results

The trained `my-react-agent-lora` was evaluated on the full held-out 153-task benchmark (`react_ts_css_eval_set_combined.jsonl`) via `agent_loop.py`, running for **16.17 hours** on the RTX 4050 GPU.

```powershell
python agent_loop.py --model my-react-agent-lora --eval-set react_ts_css_eval_set_combined.jsonl
```

### Headline Metrics

| Metric | Count | Rate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1-Shot Pass Rate (Turn 1)** | 60 / 153 | **39.2%** |
| **Self-Corrected (Turn 2+)** | +18 / 153 | **+11.8%** |
| **Final Agentic Pass Rate** | **78 / 153** | **51.0%** |
| Failed (all 5 turns exhausted) | 75 / 153 | 49.0% |
| Average Turns Used (passing tasks) | — | 1.31 turns |

**Self-correction added +11.8 percentage points** on top of the base 1-shot rate — confirming that the agentic loop with live test feedback provides meaningful gains beyond a single-turn generation.

### Per-Category Breakdown

| Check Category | Description | Pass | 1-Shot | Self-Corrected |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `tsc_and_render` | TSC + render sanity | **30/42 (71%)** | 24 | 6 |
| `tsc_render_a11y` | TSC + render + accessibility | **3/4 (75%)** | 2 | 1 |
| `tsc_render_interact` | TSC + render + user interactions | 21/58 **(36%)** | 14 | 7 |
| `tsc_only` | TypeScript compilation only | 24/49 **(49%)** | 20 | 4 |

The model is strongest on static structure + render tasks (71%), and weakest on interactive UI tests (36%) that require correct state transitions, DOM event handling, and exact ARIA attribute targeting.

### Turns Distribution (Passed Tasks Only)

| Turns Used | Tasks |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1 turn (1-shot) | 60 |
| 2 turns | 12 |
| 3 turns | 5 |
| 4 turns | 1 |

### Failure Taxonomy (75 Failing Tasks)

After analyzing the final `<observation>` from each exhausted-turn failure:

| Root Cause Cluster | Count | Pct |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TS: Unknown TSC failure** (complex multi-error TSC) | 33 | 44.0% |
| **TS: Undeclared identifier** (TS2304 — variable never declared) | 10 | 13.3% |
| **Test: Assertion failed** (wrong value / behavior) | 9 | 12.0% |
| **TS: Other parse/syntax** (TS1005, TS1109, TS1700, TS1701, etc.) | 8 | 10.7% |
| **Test: TypeError at runtime** (bad method call / null deref) | 4 | 5.3% |
| **Test: Element not found in DOM** (missing aria / testid) | 3 | 4.0% |
| **TS: Property does not exist** (TS2339) | 2 | 2.7% |
| Other isolated TS errors (TS2536, TS2315, TS2731, TS2345, etc.) | 6 | 8.0% |

### Failure Pattern Deep-Dive

**1. TS Unknown TSC Failure (33 tasks — biggest cluster)**
Dominant in `tsc_render_interact` (20/33) and `tsc_and_render` (7/33). The model generates syntactically plausible code that trips on multi-layered type errors it cannot resolve by turn 5. These include complex generic constraints on `DataTable`, `KanbanBoard`, `FormProvider`, and `FormWizard` where the component's internal state generics don't satisfy the test harness's type assertions.

**2. TS: Undeclared Identifier (10 tasks)**
The model references identifiers that were never declared in the same scope. Examples:
- `useQueryParams` references `parsedUrl`, `queryParamsToString`, `queryString` — none declared.
- `useCart` references cart state management variables from a non-existent import.
- `useConfirm` references `createPortal` without importing it.
Strategy: Use 3rd-party import rewriting to force model into self-contained code.

**3. Test Assertion Failures (9 tasks)**
The model's logic is close but produces wrong values. Examples:
- `useMediaQuery` returns `false` before `matchMedia` mock fires.
- `Slider` computes percentage incorrectly (off-by-one on boundary).
- `useIsMounted` returns stale ref value due to missing cleanup.
These are ideal targets for DPO pairs — the failing code vs. a corrected version.

**4. TS Parse/Syntax errors (8 tasks)**
TS1005 ("`;` expected") and TS1109 ("Expression expected") — the model generates truncated or malformed output, especially on complex hooks (`useUndo`, `useCart`, `useOnClickOutside`) where the code body is long enough to hit the `max_new_tokens=768` ceiling and gets cut off mid-statement.

## 11. Key Lessons Learned for 3B SLM Fine-Tuning


| Area | What Failed | What Succeeded |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Action Protocol** | JSON tool schemas (parse errors, escaping bugs). | Plain XML tags (`<thought>`, `<tool_call>`, `<finish>`). |
| **Loss Computation** | Unmasked loss across system prompts and observations. | `train_on_responses_only`: loss computed solely on assistant turns. |
| **Data Cleanliness** | Including non-agent prompt-response pairs in agentic corpus. | Strict trajectory validation: must call `write_component` and pass tests before `<finish>`. |
| **Eval Integrity** | Training on prompts from the eval benchmark. | Complete disjointness between training task banks and benchmark tasks. |
| **Test Harness** | Allowing tests to declare arbitrary top-level imports. | Centralized test import stripping (`strip_test_imports`) with global bindings injection. |
| **Sampling Strategy** | Fixed low temperature when model gets stuck in repetitive errors. | Dynamic Anti-Stuck escalation (raising temp & rep_penalty on repeated errors). |
| **Pipeline Reliability**| In-memory trajectory accumulation until script end. | Immediate incremental disk flushing + automatic `--resume` support. |

chicken, menma, scallion</item>\n    <item name=\"Vegan Shiitake\" price=\"$14\">Shiitake-kombu broth, tofu, mushrooms, seasonal greens</item>\n  </menu_category>\n  <menu_category name=\"Sides\">\n marble soda</item>\n    <item name=\"Asahi Draft\" price=\"$8\">Japanese lager, 425ml</item>\n    <item name=\"Iced Genmaicha\" price=\"$5\">Roasted brown rice green tea</item>\n  </menu_category>\n Start with the first section now.\n\nFIRST SECTION REQUIRED: Write the Header section: a sticky navigation bar with the business name/logo on the left and navigation links (Home, Menu, About, Contact) on the right. Files: src/components/Header.tsx + src/components/Header.css"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<thought>\nBuilding the Miso & Soul header. Ramen bars benefit from a dark, moody, restaurant-noir feel, so I'm using near-black background with a subtle red accent border that appears on scroll. The logo uses the Noto Serif JP heading font for an authentic Japanese typographic touch, while nav links stay in Inter for legibility.\n</thought>\n<tool_call name=\"write_site\">\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.tsx\">\nimport React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';\nimport './Header.css';\n\nexport function Header() {\n  const [scrolled, setScrolled] = useState(false);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const onScroll = () => setScrolled(window.scrollY > 16);\n    window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll);\n    return () => window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll);\n  }, []);\n\n  return (\n    <header className={`ms-header${scrolled ? ' ms-header--scrolled' : ''}`}>\n      <div className=\"ms-header__inner\">\n        <a href=\"#\" className=\"ms-header__logo\">Miso &amp; Soul</a>\n        <nav className=\"ms-header__nav\" aria-label=\"Main navigation\">\n          <a href=\"#hero\" className=\"ms-header__link\">Home</a>\n          <a href=\"#menu\" className=\"ms-header__link\">Menu</a>\n          <a href=\"#footer\" className=\"ms-header__link\">Contact</a>\n        </nav>\n      </div>\n    </header>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.css\">\n.ms-header {\n  position: sticky;\n  top: 0;\n  z-index: 100;\n  width: 100%;\n  background: rgba(13, 13, 13, 0.9);\n  backdrop-filter: blur(10px);\n  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(220, 38, 38, 0.15);\n  transition: box-shadow 0.3s ease, background 0.3s ease;\n}\n.ms-header--scrolled {\n  background: rgba(13, 13, 13, 0.98);\n  box-shadow: 0 4px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);\n}\n.ms-header__inner {\n  max-width: 1180px;\n  margin: 0 auto;\n  padding: 0 2rem;\n  height: 70px;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n}\n.ms-header__logo {\n  font-family: 'Noto Serif JP', serif;\n  font-size: 1.3rem;\n  font-weight: 700;\n  color: #f5f5f4;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  letter-spacing: 0.02em;\n}\n.ms-header__nav {\n  display: flex;\n  gap: 2rem;\n}\n.ms-header__link {\n  color: #a8a29e;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  font-size: 0.88rem;\n  font-weight: 500;\n  letter-spacing: 0.04em;\n  text-transform: uppercase;\n  transition: color 0.2s;\n  position: relative;\n}\n.ms-header__link:hover { color: #dc2626; }\n@media (max-width: 700px) {\n  .ms-header__nav { gap: 1.1rem; }\n  .ms-header__logo { font-size: 1.1rem; }\n}\n</file>\n</tool_call>"}, {"role": "user", "content": "<observation status=\"ok\">\n[Files accepted]:\n  \u2713 src/components/Header.tsx\n  \u2713 src/components/Header.css\n\n[NEXT SECTION REQUIRED]: Write the Hero section: a full-width banner with a background image or gradient, the business tagline as an h1, a subheading, and a prominent CTA button. Files: src/components/Menu.tsx + src/components/Menu.css\nWrite ONE <tool_call name=\"write_site\"> with exactly one .tsx file and one .css file for this section.\n</observation>"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<thought>\nWith three menu categories in the brief (Ramen, Sides, Drinks), a tabbed interface keeps things scannable instead of one long scroll. Prices stay in the red accent color for quick visual scanning, and cards get a subtle red glow on hover to tie back to the header/hero palette.\n</thought>\n<tool_call name=\"write_site\">\n<file path=\"src/components/Menu.tsx\">\nimport React, { useState } from 'react';\nimport './Menu.css';\n\ninterface MenuItem { name: string; price: string; description: string; }\ninterface MenuCategory { name: string; items: MenuItem[]; }\n\nconst MENU_DATA: MenuCategory[] = [\n  {\n    name: 'Ramen',\n    items: [\n      { name: 'Tonkotsu Classic', price: '$16', description: '18-hour pork bone broth, chashu, ajitama, nori' },\n      { name: 'Spicy Miso', price: '$17', description: 'Fermented miso broth, ground pork, chili oil, corn' },\n      { name: 'Shoyu Chicken', price: '$15', description: 'Clear soy broth, roast chicken, menma, scallion' },\n      { name: 'Vegan Shiitake', price: '$14', description: 'Shiitake-kombu broth, tofu, mushrooms, seasonal greens' },\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    name: 'Sides',\n    items: [\n      { name: 'Karaage', price: '$9', description: 'Japanese fried chicken thigh, yuzu kosho mayo' },\n      { name: 'Gyoza (5pc)', price: '$8', description: 'Pan-seared pork dumplings, chili vinegar' },\n      { name: 'Steamed Bao (2pc)', price: '$7', description: 'Pork belly, hoisin, pickled cucumber' },\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    name: 'Drinks',\n    items: [\n      { name: 'Ramune', price: '$4', description: 'Classic Japanese marble soda' },\n      { name: 'Asahi Draft', price: '$8', description: 'Japanese lager, 425ml' },\n      { name: 'Iced Genmaicha', price: '$5', description: 'Roasted brown rice green tea' },\n    ],\n  },\n];\n\nexport function Menu() {\n  const [active, setActive] = useState('Ramen');\n  const current = MENU_DATA.find(c => c.name === active) ?? MENU_DATA[0];\n\n  return (\n    <section className=\"ms-menu\" id=\"menu\" aria-labelledby=\"ms-menu-heading\">\n      <div className=\"ms-menu__inner\">\n        <div className=\"ms-menu__header\">\n          <p className=\"ms-menu__eyebrow\">The Menu</p>\n          <h2 id=\"ms-menu-heading\" className=\"ms-menu__title\">Bowls Worth the Wait</h2>\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"ms-menu__tabs\" role=\"tablist\" aria-label=\"Menu categories\">\n          {MENU_DATA.map(cat => (\n            <button\n              key={cat.name}\n              role=\"tab\"\n              aria-selected={active === cat.name}\n              className={`ms-menu__tab${active === cat.name ? ' ms-menu__tab--active' : ''}`}\n              onClick={() => setActive(cat.name)}\n            >\n              {cat.name}\n            </button>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"ms-menu__grid\" role=\"tabpanel\" aria-label={current.name}>\n          {current.items.map(item => (\n            <article key={item.name} className=\"ms-menu__card\">\n              <div className=\"ms-menu__card-top\">\n                <h3 className=\"ms-menu__item-name\">{item.name}</h3>\n                <span className=\"ms-menu__item-price\">{item.price}</span>\n              </div>\n              <p className=\"ms-menu__item-desc\">{item.description}</p>\n            </article>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n      </div>\n    </section>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Menu.css\">\n.ms-menu {\n  padding: 6.5rem 2rem;\n  background: #141414;\n}\n.ms-menu__inner { max-width: 1080px; margin: 0 auto; }\n.ms-menu__header { text-align: center; margin-bottom: 3rem; }\n.ms-menu__eyebrow {\n  font-size: 0.75rem;\n  font-weight: 700;\n  letter-spacing: 0.2em;\n  text-transform: uppercase;\n  color: #dc2626;\n  margin: 0 0 0.75rem;\n}\n.ms-menu__title {\n  font-family: 'Noto Serif JP', serif;\n  font-size: clamp(1.9rem, 3.8vw, 2.75rem);\n  color: #fafaf9;\n  margin: 0;\n}\n.ms-menu__tabs {\n  display: flex;\n  justify-content: center;\n  gap: 0.5rem;\n  margin-bottom: 3rem;\n  flex-wrap: wrap;\n}\n.ms-menu__tab {\n  padding: 0.55rem 1.4rem;\n  border: 2px solid #292524;\n  background: transparent;\n  color: #a8a29e;\n  border-radius: 2rem;\n  font-size: 0.88rem;\n  font-weight: 600;\n  cursor: pointer;\n  transition: all 0.2s;\n}\n.ms-menu__tab:hover { border-color: #dc2626; color: #dc2626; }\n.ms-menu__tab--active { background: #dc2626; border-color: #dc2626; color: #fafaf9; }\n.ms-menu__grid {\n  display: grid;\n  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(280px, 1fr));\n  gap: 1.1rem;\n}\n.ms-menu__card {\n  background: #1c1917;\n  border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);\n  border-radius: 10px;\n  padding: 1.4rem;\n  transition: transform 0.2s, border-color 0.2s;\n}\n.ms-menu__card:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); border-color: rgba(220,38,38,0.3); }\n.ms-menu__card-top {\n  display: flex;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n  gap: 1rem;\n  margin-bottom: 0.6rem;\n}\n.ms-menu__item-name {\n  font-family: 'Noto Serif JP', serif;\n  font-size: 1.05rem;\n  color: #fafaf9;\n  margin: 0;\n}\n.ms-menu__item-price { font-weight: 700; color: #dc2626; white-space: nowrap; }\n.ms-menu__item-desc { font-size: 0.87rem; color: #78716c; margin: 0; line-height: 1.6; }\n</file>\n</tool_call>"}, {"role": "user", "content": "<observation status=\"ok\">\n[Files accepted]:\n  \u2713 src/components/Menu.tsx\n  \u2713 src/components/Menu.css\n\n[NEXT SECTION REQUIRED]: Write the Footer section: a dark background footer with the business name, brief nav links, contact info (address, phone, email, hours), and a copyright notice. All rights reserved.</p>\n      </div>\n    </footer>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Footer.css\">\n.ms-footer {\n  background: #0a0a0a;\n  border-top: 1px solid rgba(220,38,38,0.2);\n  padding: 4.5rem 2rem 0;\n}\n.ms-footer__inner {\n  max-width: 1080px;\n  margin: 0 auto;\n  display: grid;\n  grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr 1.5fr;\n  gap: 3rem;\n  padding-bottom: 2.5rem;\n  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);\n}\n.ms-footer__logo {\n  font-family: 'Noto Serif JP', serif;\n  font-size: 1.3rem;\n  color: #dc2626;\n  margin: 0 0 0.5rem;\n}\n.ms-footer__tagline { font-size: 0.88rem; color: #57534e; margin: 0; max-width: 260px; line-height: 1.6; }\n.ms-footer__nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.6rem; }\n.ms-footer__heading {\n  font-size: 0.7rem;\n  font-weight: 700;\n  letter-spacing: 0.14em;\n  text-transform: uppercase;\n  color: #dc2626;\n  margin: 0 0 0.75rem;\n}\n.ms-footer__link { color: #a8a29e; text-decoration: none; font-size: 0.88rem; display: block; transition: color 0.2s; }\n.ms-footer__link:hover { color: #fafaf9; }\n.ms-footer__contact { font-style: normal; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; color: #a8a29e; font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.6; }\n.ms-footer__hours { color: #57534e; font-size: 0.82rem; }\n.ms-footer__bottom {\n  max-width: 1080px;\n  margin: 0 auto;\n  padding: 1.5rem 0;\n  text-align: center;\n  font-size: 0.78rem;\n  color: #292524;\n}\n@media (max-width: 700px) {\n  .ms-footer__inner { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 2rem; }\n}\n</file>\n</tool_call>"}, {"role": "user", "content": "<observation status=\"complete\">\n[SITE BUILD COMPLETE]: All required sections have been written successfully.\n[Files written in this session]:\n  \u2713 src/components/Header.tsx\n  \u2713 src/components/Header.css\n  \u2713 src/components/Hero.tsx\n  \u2713 src/components/Hero.css\n  \u2713 src/components/Menu.tsx\n  \u2713 src/components/Menu.css\n  \u2713 src/components/Footer.tsx\n  \u2713 src/components/Footer.css\nOutput a <finish> tag with a brief summary of the site you built.\n</observation>"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<thought>\nAll four sections were accepted: Header, Hero, Menu, and Footer, each using the near-black/red palette and Noto Serif JP headings from the brief.\n</thought>\n<finish>\nBuilt the complete Miso & Soul ramen bar website with 4 sections:\n- Header: sticky dark nav with logo and links\n- Hero: full-viewport ramen photo banner with tagline and CTA\n- Menu: tabbed Ramen/Sides/Drinks categories with all items from the brief\n- Footer: brand, nav, and full contact info\nColor scheme: near-black (#0d0d0d) with red (#dc2626) accent, Noto Serif JP headings.\n</finish>"}]}
{"task_id": "site_event_devsummit_2025", "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are an expert autonomous React, TypeScript, and CSS coding agent specialising in full-page website composition.\nYour objective is to build a complete, visually rich, multi-section website from a structured content brief, one section at a time.\n\nYou interact with an automated build environment using structured XML tags:\n\n1. <thought>\nExplain your plan for the current section, describe styling decisions, and acknowledge the content brief.\n</thought>\n\n2. <tool_call name=\"write_site\">\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.tsx\">\n// Complete React + TypeScript component for this section\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.css\">\n/* Required CSS \u2014 NEVER leave empty. Every section MUST have visual styles. */\n</file>\n</tool_call>\nWrites ONE section (one .tsx file + one .css file) per turn. Do not invent or alter content.\n- Do NOT output markdown code fences (```) around your <tool_call> tags.\n- Do NOT combine multiple sections into one turn \u2014 one section per tool_call only.\n"}, {"role": "user", "content": "Build a complete website for the following brief.\n\n<content_brief>\n  <business_name>DevSummit 2025</business_name>\n  <tagline>Where builders come to level up</tagline>\n  <business_type>event</business_type>\n  <primary_color>#030712</primary_color>\n  <accent_color>#2563eb</accent_color>\n  <font_heading>Inter</font_heading>\n  <font_body>Inter</font_body>\n  <sections>header, hero, speakers, schedule, footer</sections>\n  <speaker name=\"Sarah Chen\" role=\"Staff Engineer, Stripe\" />\n  <speaker name=\"Marcus Odom\" role=\"VP Engineering, Vercel\" />\n  <speaker name=\"Ayesha Khan\" role=\"Principal Researcher, DeepMind\" />\n  <speaker name=\"Diego Fuentes\" role=\"Founder, OpenRuntime\" />\n  <schedule_track name=\"Morning Keynotes\" time=\"9:00am - 12:00pm\" description=\"Opening keynotes on the future of developer tooling and platform engineering.\" />\n  <schedule_track name=\"Afternoon Workshops\" time=\"1:00pm - 5:00pm\" description=\"Hands-on workshops covering distributed systems, AI infra, and dev experience.\" />\n  <schedule_track name=\"Evening Networking\" time=\"6:00pm - 9:00pm\" description=\"Sponsor showcase, drinks, and structured networking by track.\" />\n  <contact>\n    <location>Sydney Convention Centre</location>\n    <dates>April 12-13, 2025</dates>\n    <email>tickets@devsummit.io</email>\n  </contact>\n</content_brief>\n\nYou will build the site ONE SECTION AT A TIME. Start with the first section now.\n\nFIRST SECTION REQUIRED: Write the Header section: a sticky navigation bar with the event name/logo on the left, nav links (Speakers, Schedule, Contact) on the right, and a 'Get Tickets' CTA button. Files: src/components/Header.tsx + src/components/Header.css"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<thought>\nFor a developer conference the header should feel technical and confident: near-black background, a bold two-tone logo (name in white, year in the blue accent), and a single high-contrast 'Get Tickets' CTA since ticket conversion is the header's main job.\n</thought>\n<tool_call name=\"write_site\">\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.tsx\">\nimport React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';\nimport './Header.css';\n\nexport function Header() {\n  const [scrolled, setScrolled] = useState(false);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const onScroll = () => setScrolled(window.scrollY > 12);\n    window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll);\n    return () => window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll);\n  }, []);\n\n  return (\n    <header className={`ds-header${scrolled ? ' ds-header--scrolled' : ''}`}>\n      <div className=\"ds-header__inner\">\n        <a href=\"#\" className=\"ds-header__logo\">DevSummit<span className=\"ds-header__year\">2025</span></a>\n        <nav className=\"ds-header__nav\" aria-label=\"Main navigation\">\n          <a href=\"#speakers\" className=\"ds-header__link\">Speakers</a>\n          <a href=\"#schedule\" className=\"ds-header__link\">Schedule</a>\n          <a href=\"#footer\" className=\"ds-header__link\">Contact</a>\n        </nav>\n        <a href=\"mailto:tickets@devsummit.io\" className=\"ds-header__cta\">Get Tickets</a>\n      </div>\n    </header>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.css\">\n.ds-header {\n  position: sticky;\n  top: 0;\n  z-index: 100;\n  width: 100%;\n  background: rgba(3, 7, 18, 0.85);\n  backdrop-filter: blur(14px);\n  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.15);\n  transition: background 0.3s, box-shadow 0.3s;\n}\n.ds-header--scrolled {\n  background: rgba(3, 7, 18, 0.97);\n  box-shadow: 0 4px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.5);\n}\n.ds-header__inner {\n  max-width: 1240px;\n  margin: 0 auto;\n  padding: 0 2rem;\n  height: 68px;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n  gap: 1.5rem;\n}\n.ds-header__logo {\n  font-weight: 800;\n  font-size: 1.1rem;\n  color: #f8fafc;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  letter-spacing: -0.02em;\n}\n.ds-header__year { color: #2563eb; margin-left: 0.25rem; }\n.ds-header__nav { display: flex; gap: 1.75rem; align-items: center; }\n.ds-header__link {\n  color: #94a3b8;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  font-size: 0.9rem;\n  font-weight: 500;\n  transition: color 0.2s;\n}\n.ds-header__link:hover { color: #f8fafc; }\n.ds-header__cta {\n  padding: 0.5rem 1.2rem;\n  background: #2563eb;\n  color: #f8fafc;\n  border-radius: 6px;\n  font-size: 0.85rem;\n  font-weight: 700;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  white-space: nowrap;\n  transition: background 0.2s, transform 0.15s;\n}\n.ds-header__cta:hover { background: #3b82f6; Files: src/components/Hero.tsx + src/components/Hero.css\nWrite ONE <tool_call name=\"write_site\"> with exactly one .tsx file and one .css file for this section.\n</observation>"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<thought>\nThe hero needs to establish credibility fast. I'm using a subtle animated grid background (pure CSS gradients, no images) which reads as 'technical conference' immediately, a pulsing badge with the exact date and venue from the brief, and the tagline as a large bold h1.\n</thought>\n<tool_call name=\"write_site\">\n<file path=\"src/components/Hero.tsx\">\nimport React from 'react';\nimport './Hero.css';\n\nexport function Hero() {\n  return (\n    <section className=\"ds-hero\" id=\"hero\">\n      <div className=\"ds-hero__grid\" aria-hidden=\"true\" />\n      <div className=\"ds-hero__content\">\n        <div className=\"ds-hero__badge\">\n          <span className=\"ds-hero__badge-dot\" aria-hidden=\"true\" />\n          April 12&ndash;13, 2025 &middot; Sydney Convention Centre\n        </div>\n        <h1 className=\"ds-hero__title\">Where builders come to level up</h1>\n        <p className=\"ds-hero__subtitle\">\n          Two days of keynotes, hands-on workshops, and networking with the engineers\n          building the tools you use every day.\n        </p>\n        <a href=\"mailto:tickets@devsummit.io\" className=\"ds-hero__cta\">Reserve Your Seat</a>\n      </div>\n    </section>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Hero.css\">\n.ds-hero {\n  position: relative;\n  min-height: 88vh;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: center;\n  overflow: hidden;\n  background: #030712;\n}\n.ds-hero__grid {\n  position: absolute;\n  inset: 0;\n  background-image:\n    linear-gradient(rgba(37,99,235,0.08) 1px, transparent 1px),\n    linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(37,99,235,0.08) 1px, transparent 1px);\n  background-size: 48px 48px;\n  mask-image: radial-gradient(ellipse at center, black 20%, transparent 75%);\n}\n.ds-hero__content {\n  position: relative;\n  z-index: 1;\n  max-width: 760px;\n  padding: 2rem;\n  text-align: center;\n}\n.ds-hero__badge {\n  display: inline-flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  gap: 0.5rem;\n  padding: 0.4rem 1rem;\n  border-radius: 2rem;\n  background: rgba(37,99,235,0.1);\n  border: 1px solid rgba(37,99,235,0.3);\n  font-size: 0.85rem;\n  color: #93c5fd;\n  font-weight: 500;\n  margin-bottom: 1.75rem;\n}\n.ds-hero__badge-dot {\n  width: 6px; Files: src/components/Speakers.tsx + src/components/Speakers.css\nWrite ONE <tool_call name=\"write_site\"> with exactly one .tsx file and one .css file for this section.\n</observation>"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<thought>\nFor the 4 speakers I'm using a clean 4-column grid with generated initials avatars (gradient circles) instead of missing photos, since no images were provided in the brief. ' bl-header--solid' : ''}`}>\n      <div className=\"bl-header__inner\">\n        <a href=\"#\" className=\"bl-header__logo\">BLANC STUDIO</a>\n        <nav className=\"bl-header__nav\" aria-label=\"Main navigation\">\n          <a href=\"#hero\" className=\"bl-header__link\">Home</a>\n          <a href=\"#products\" className=\"bl-header__link\">Collection</a>\n          <a href=\"#footer\" className=\"bl-header__link\">Contact</a>\n        </nav>\n      </div>\n    </header>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.css\">\n.bl-header {\n  position: sticky;\n  top: 0;\n  z-index: 100;\n  width: 100%;\n  background: rgba(250, 250, 249, 0.6);\n  backdrop-filter: blur(8px);\n  border-bottom: 1px solid transparent;\n  transition: background 0.3s, border-color 0.3s;\n}\n.bl-header--solid {\n  background: rgba(250, 250, 249, 0.96);\n  border-bottom-color: rgba(28, 25, 23, 0.08);\n}\n.bl-header__inner {\n  max-width: 1200px;\n  margin: 0 auto;\n  padding: 0 2rem;\n  height: 84px;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n}\n.bl-header__logo {\n  font-family: 'Cormorant Garamond', serif;\n  font-size: 1.4rem;\n  font-weight: 600;\n  letter-spacing: 0.18em;\n  color: #1c1917;\n  text-decoration: none;\n}\n.bl-header__nav { display: flex; price: string; category: string; }\n\nconst PRODUCTS: Product[] = [\n  { name: 'Linen Wrap Dress', price: '$320', category: 'Dresses' },\n  { name: 'Cashmere Turtleneck', price: '$480', category: 'Knitwear' },\n  { name: 'Tailored Blazer', price: '$560', category: 'Outerwear' },\n  { name: 'Wide-Leg Trousers', price: '$290', category: 'Bottoms' },\n  { name: 'Silk Cami', price: '$180', category: 'Tops' },\n  { name: 'Merino Coat', price: '$720', category: 'Outerwear' },\n];\n\nexport function Products() {\n  return (\n    <section className=\"bl-products\" id=\"products\" aria-labelledby=\"bl-products-heading\">\n      <div className=\"bl-products__inner\">\n        <div className=\"bl-products__header\">\n          <p className=\"bl-products__eyebrow\">Shop</p>\n          <h2 id=\"bl-products-heading\" className=\"bl-products__title\">Featured Pieces</h2>\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"bl-products__grid\">\n          {PRODUCTS.map(p => (\n            <article key={p.name} className=\"bl-product-card\">\n              <div className=\"bl-product-card__image\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n                <span className=\"bl-product-card__tag\">{p.category}</span>\n              </div>\n              <h3 className=\"bl-product-card__name\">{p.name}</h3>\n              <p className=\"bl-product-card__price\">{p.price}</p>\n            </article>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n      </div>\n    </section>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Products.css\">\n.bl-products {\n  padding: 6.5rem 2rem;\n  background: #fafaf9;\n}\n.bl-products__inner { max-width: 1180px; color: #78716c; margin: 0; }\n@media (max-width: 900px) { .bl-products__grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); } }\n@media (max-width: 560px) { .bl-products__grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; Nothing competes with the work shown further down the page.\n</thought>\n<tool_call name=\"write_site\">\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.tsx\">\nimport React from 'react';\nimport './Header.css';\n\nexport function Header() {\n  return (\n    <header className=\"mb-header\" role=\"banner\">\n      <div className=\"mb-header__inner\">\n        <a href=\"#\" className=\"mb-header__name\">Marcus Bell</a>\n        <nav className=\"mb-header__nav\" aria-label=\"Main navigation\">\n          <a href=\"#projects\" className=\"mb-header__link\">Projects</a>\n          <a href=\"#contact\" className=\"mb-header__link\">Contact</a>\n        </nav>\n      </div>\n    </header>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.css\">\n.mb-header {\n  position: sticky;\n  top: 0;\n  z-index: 100;\n  width: 100%;\n  background: rgba(12, 12, 12, 0.85);\n  backdrop-filter: blur(10px);\n  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(249, 115, 22, 0.12);\n}\n.mb-header__inner {\n  max-width: 980px;\n  margin: 0 auto;\n  padding: 0 2rem;\n  height: 66px;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n}\n.mb-header__name {\n  font-weight: 700;\n  font-size: 1.05rem;\n  color: #f5f5f4;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  letter-spacing: -0.01em;\n}\n.mb-header__nav { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; }\n.mb-header__link {\n  padding: 0.4rem 0.9rem;\n  color: #a3a3a3;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  font-size: 0.88rem;\n  font-weight: 500;\n  border-radius: 6px;\n  transition: color 0.2s, background 0.2s;\n}\n.mb-header__link:hover { color: #f97316; background: rgba(249,115,22,0.08); }\n</file>\n</tool_call>"}, {"role": "user", "content": "<observation status=\"ok\">\n[Files accepted]:\n  \u2713 src/components/Header.tsx\n  \u2713 src/components/Header.css\n\n[NEXT SECTION REQUIRED]: Write the Hero section: name/title intro with an animated typing role text that cycles through 3 roles using pure CSS, a short bio, and CTA buttons. Files: src/components/Hero.tsx + src/components/Hero.css\nWrite ONE <tool_call name=\"write_site\"> with exactly one .tsx file and one .css file for this section.\n</observation>"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<thought>\nThe animated role text is built with a pure-CSS vertical-cycle animation: three role labels stacked in a fixed-height, overflow-hidden container, translated up on a keyframe loop with steps(1) so each role holds fully before the next appears (no third-party libraries needed). I kept the visible aria-label static for accessibility so screen readers get the full role list.\n</thought>\n<tool_call name=\"write_site\">\n<file path=\"src/components/Hero.tsx\">\nimport React from 'react';\nimport './Hero.css';\n\nexport function Hero() {\n  return (\n    <section className=\"mb-hero\" id=\"hero\" aria-labelledby=\"mb-hero-name\">\n      <div className=\"mb-hero__inner\">\n        <p className=\"mb-hero__greeting\">Hi, I&apos;m</p>\n        <h1 id=\"mb-hero-name\" className=\"mb-hero__name\">Marcus Bell</h1>\n        <p className=\"mb-hero__roles\" aria-label=\"UX Designer, Product Strategist, Design Systems Lead\">\n          <span className=\"mb-hero__role-cycle\">\n            <span>UX Designer</span>\n            <span>Product Strategist</span>\n            <span>Design Systems Lead</span>\n          </span>\n        </p>\n        <p className=\"mb-hero__bio\">\n          I turn ambiguous product problems into clear, usable interfaces &mdash;\n          from early strategy through pixel-level execution.\n        </p>\n        <div className=\"mb-hero__actions\">\n          <a href=\"#projects\" className=\"mb-hero__btn mb-hero__btn--primary\">View Projects</a>\n          <a href=\"#contact\" className=\"mb-hero__btn mb-hero__btn--secondary\">Get in Touch</a>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n    </section>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Hero.css\">\n.mb-hero {\n  padding: 8rem 2rem 5.5rem;\n  background: #0c0c0c;\n  text-align: center;\n}\n.mb-hero__inner { max-width: 640px; margin: 0 auto; }\n.mb-hero__greeting {\n  font-size: 0.95rem;\n  color: #f97316;\n  margin: 0 0 0.5rem;\n  font-weight: 600;\n}\n.mb-hero__name {\n  font-size: clamp(2.4rem, 5.5vw, 3.75rem);\n  font-weight: 800;\n  color: #f5f5f4;\n  margin: 0 0 1rem;\n  letter-spacing: -0.03em;\n}\n.mb-hero__roles {\n  height: 1.8rem;\n  overflow: hidden;\n  margin: 0 0 1.75rem;\n}\n.mb-hero__role-cycle {\n  display: flex;\n  flex-direction: column;\n  animation: mb-cycle 6s steps(1) infinite;\n}\n.mb-hero__role-cycle span {\n  font-size: 1.2rem;\n  font-weight: 600;\n  color: #d4d4d4;\n  height: 1.8rem;\n  line-height: 1.8rem;\n}\n@keyframes mb-cycle {\n  0%, 30% { transform: translateY(0); }\n  33%, 63% { transform: translateY(-1.8rem); }\n  66%, 96% { transform: translateY(-3.6rem); }\n  100% { transform: translateY(0); }\n}\n.mb-hero__bio {\n  font-size: 1.02rem;\n  color: #737373;\n  line-height: 1.75;\n  margin: 0 auto 2.25rem;\n  max-width: 480px;\n}\n.mb-hero__actions { display: flex; justify-content: center; gap: 0.75rem; flex-wrap: wrap; }\n.mb-hero__btn {\n  padding: 0.75rem 1.6rem;\n  border-radius: 8px;\n  font-weight: 700;\n  font-size: 0.9rem;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  transition: all 0.2s;\n}\n.mb-hero__btn--primary { background: #f97316; flex-direction: column; }\n.mb-proj-card {\n  display: flex;\n  gap: 1.75rem;\n  padding: 1.75rem 0;\n  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.07);\n  transition: padding-left 0.25s;\n}\n.mb-proj-card:hover { padding-left: 0.5rem; Start with the first section now.\n\nFIRST SECTION REQUIRED: Write the Header section: a sticky nav with the organization name on the left, links (Our Work, Impact, Contact) on the right, and a 'Donate' CTA button. Files: src/components/Header.tsx + src/components/Header.css"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<thought>\nEnvironmental nonprofits need to feel grounded and trustworthy rather than flashy, so I used a deep forest-green background with a single lime-green accent reserved almost entirely for the Donate button, making the action the most visually urgent element in the header.\n</thought>\n<tool_call name=\"write_site\">\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.tsx\">\nimport React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';\nimport './Header.css';\n\nexport function Header() {\n  const [scrolled, setScrolled] = useState(false);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const onScroll = () => setScrolled(window.scrollY > 16);\n    window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll);\n    return () => window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll);\n  }, []);\n\n  return (\n    <header className={`gh-header${scrolled ? ' gh-header--scrolled' : ''}`}>\n      <div className=\"gh-header__inner\">\n        <a href=\"#\" className=\"gh-header__logo\">Green Horizon Alliance</a>\n        <nav className=\"gh-header__nav\" aria-label=\"Main navigation\">\n          <a href=\"#hero\" className=\"gh-header__link\">Our Work</a>\n          <a href=\"#impact\" className=\"gh-header__link\">Impact</a>\n          <a href=\"#footer\" className=\"gh-header__link\">Contact</a>\n        </nav>\n        <a href=\"mailto:connect@greenhorizonalliance.org\" className=\"gh-header__cta\">Donate</a>\n      </div>\n    </header>\n  );\n}\n</file>\n<file path=\"src/components/Header.css\">\n.gh-header {\n  position: sticky;\n  top: 0;\n  z-index: 100;\n  width: 100%;\n  background: rgba(11, 31, 20, 0.9);\n  backdrop-filter: blur(10px);\n  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(132, 204, 22, 0.15);\n  transition: box-shadow 0.3s;\n}\n.gh-header--scrolled { box-shadow: 0 4px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.35); }\n.gh-header__inner {\n  max-width: 1180px;\n  margin: 0 auto;\n  padding: 0 2rem;\n  height: 70px;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n  gap: 1.5rem;\n}\n.gh-header__logo {\n  font-family: 'Merriweather', serif;\n  font-size: 1.1rem;\n  font-weight: 700;\n  color: #f0fdf4;\n  text-decoration: none;\n}\n.gh-header__nav { display: flex; gap: 1.75rem; }\n.gh-header__link {\n  color: #a7bfae;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  font-size: 0.88rem;\n  font-weight: 500;\n  transition: color 0.2s;\n}\n.gh-header__link:hover { color: #84cc16; }\n.gh-header__cta {\n  padding: 0.5rem 1.25rem;\n  background: #84cc16;\n  color: #0b1f14;\n  border-radius: 6px;\n  font-size: 0.85rem;\n  font-weight: 700;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  white-space: nowrap;\n  transition: background 0.2s, transform 0.15s;\n}\n.gh-header__cta:hover { background: #a3e635; transform: translateY(-1px); }\n@media (max-width: 680px) { .gh-header__nav { display: none; } }\n</file>\n</tool_call>"}, {"role": "user", "content": "<observation status=\"ok\">\n[Files accepted]:\n  \u2713 src/components/Header.tsx\n  \u2713 src/components/Header.css\n\n[NEXT SECTION REQUIRED]: Write the Hero section: full-width banner with the tagline as h1, a supporting subheading, and a donate CTA. Files: src/components/Hero.tsx + src/components/Hero.css\nWrite ONE <tool_call name=\"write_site\"> with exactly one .tsx file and one .css file for this section.\n</observation>"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<thought>\nThe hero pairs a real forest photograph with a deep green gradient overlay so the lime accent color reads clearly against it. path=\"src/components/Hero.tsx\">\nimport React from 'react';\nimport './Hero.css';\n\nexport function Hero() {\n  return (\n    <section className=\"gh-hero\" id=\"hero\">\n      <div className=\"gh-hero__overlay\" aria-hidden=\"true\" />\n      <div className=\"gh-hero__content\">\n        <h1 className=\"gh-hero__title\">Restoring wild places,<br />one acre at a time</h1>\n path=\"src/components/Hero.css\">\n.gh-hero {\n  position: relative;\n  min-height: 88vh;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: center;\n  overflow: hidden;\n  background:\n    linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(11,31,20,0.9) 0%, rgba(11,31,20,0.6) 55%, rgba(132,204,22,0.1) 100%),\n    url('https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1441974231531-c6227db76b6e?w=1600&q=80') center/cover no-repeat;\n}\n.gh-hero__overlay {\n  position: absolute;\n  inset: 0;\n  background: radial-gradient(ellipse at 25% 70%, rgba(132,204,22,0.1) 0%, transparent 60%);\n  pointer-events: font-size: clamp(2.2rem, 5vw, 3.75rem);\n  font-weight: 700;\n  color: #f0fdf4;\n  line-height: 1.2;\n  margin: 0 0 1.5rem;\n}\n.gh-hero__subtitle {\n  font-size: 1.05rem;\n  color: #cbd8ce;\n
